summary: Don't waste money on products that don't work. We list the most beneficial anti-aging ingredients scientifically proven to reduce wrinkles.
body_markdown:
## Proven's Guide to The Best Anti-Aging Ingredients:


**AHA and BHAs**


Beta and Alpha Hydroxy Acids aid in removing dead skin cells to combat lines, wrinkles and spots, helping with cell turnover, to give the skin a more overall youthful appearance.


**ALPHA-LIPOIC ACID**


Adds powerful antioxidant protection and helps diminish signs of aging by reducing inflammation.


**BETA-GLUCAN**


A natural antioxidant, found in yeast. Studies have shown it to offer substantial moisture retention, helping to keep skin supple and hydrated.


**BIOTIN**


Promotes healthier hair, skin, and nails by helping to replenish vitamins found naturally in skin, but decrease with age.


**CAFFEINE**


Contains potent antioxidant properties, helps protect against UV damage to slow down the physical effects of photoaging.


**CERAMIDES**


They can help your skin maintain moisture levels, particularly beneficial for irritated, red or dry skin. Found naturally in skin, ceramides protect the skin barrier, helping it stay hydrated.


**COENZYME Q10**


Helps boost collagen production as well as elastin found naturally in your skin.


**GLYCOLIC ACID**


A derivative of sugarcane, glycolic acid acts as an exfoliant by removing dead skin cells from the surface and smoothing texture that can help reduce the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles.


**GREEN TEA**


Known for its anti-inflammatory properties, Green Tea addresses sun damage, helping to protect against further collagen breakdown.


**HYALURONIC ACID**


One of the most powerful moisturizers found in many anti-aging products, Hyaluronic Acid can hold up to 1000 times its weight in water to keep skin hydrated and supple.


**HYDROQUINONE**


Addresses uneven skin tone and discolorations caused by hormonal changes.


**JOJOBA OIL**


A natural vegetable wax extracted from the Jojoba plant, it is rich in vitamins and zinc. Addresses breakouts, undereye circles and puffiness in the eye area.


**LACTIC ACID**


Exfoliates and helps brighten skin. It can also attract and hold moisture, for a firmer look and feel in the skin.


**RED GINSENG EXTRACT**


It can help to reduce signs of UVA and UVB damage, adds moisture.


**RETINOL**


A natural and powerful antioxidant that helps reduce signs of aging by removing dead skin. Also found in anti-aging products, this ingredient helps diminish the appearance of lines and imperfections, offering improved skin texture.


**SPF**


Sun protection factor is crucial. 80% of facial aging is related to UV exposure. Sunscreen, preferably a broad spectrum with SPF 30 or higher, protects against daily exposure to free radicals and other environmental stressors.


**VITAMIN A**


contains organic compounds that include retinol and beta-carotene, replacing what we lose naturally in skin and addressing environmental damage.


**VITAMIN C**


A powerful antioxidant reduces the appearance of spots and uneven skin tone, soothes redness and inflammation.


**VITAMIN E**


A powerful antioxidant that reduces inflammation. This vitamin is not found naturally in the body so it is an important factor when choosing facial products.


While all these ingredients are beneficial, you would not use every one listed here. The best approach is a personalized skincare regimen formulated with the most beneficial ingredients for your skin. A gentle cleanser,[daily moisturizer with SPF](https://www.provenskincare.com/personalized-day-moisturizer/) and night cream with antioxidants are key and ancillary products, such as a toner or anti-aging eye cream can be added if needed.


Proven is all about personalization. It is supported by extensive research tailored to unique skin types, issues, and needs. An exclusive and targeted skin assessment focuses on lifestyle, diet, living environment and more, offering a holistic picture of a person’s skin health. This intense personalization pinpoints an individual’s skin type and concerns, determining what product formulations would be personal bests suited for him or her. And personalized products can evolve with the user’s changing issues and needs. Is your skin getting drier? Hormonal changes? Formulas can be adjusted.


For optimal skin health, a visit to a dermatologist for a yearly check is always a good idea. Book the visit. Apply that SPF. Cover up with a hat, sunglasses and long sleeves. Get at least 6 to 8 hours of sleep each night and hydrate! And, use your personalized skincare regimen each morning and evening to giving your skin the TLC it craves and deserves as it matures.
